title: What is EyeNet
text:
01  What is EyeNet  
 EyeNet is on-premises computer vision that turns ordinary cameras into vision nodes — they detect, decide, and act on site. Video stays local by default. One platform serves homes, care, offices, shops, security posts, ships, and plants. 

       
         Who buys — and why now 
         Real buyers, real jobs: each persona hits a wall with incumbents — then starts on cameras they already have and gets the outcome today. 
         
           An  HR manager  can now let every employee check in from their own PC or phone — and push grants to the ERP/CRM — with zero new hardware, even at thousands of seats. 
           A  shop or mall owner  can now prove who is watching a screen and switch the playlist on cams they already have, without a locked player kit. 
           A  parent  can now get private intrusion alerts on the home cams they already own — or a cheap everyday camera — with no cloud subscription. 
           A  parent of a student living away  can now watch a remote flat or cottage with one ordinary cam — phone pings only, no guard contract or cloud VMS. 
           A  care provider  can now turn a patient room cam into fall and help-call events for the clinical stack — without shipping cloud video. 
           A  security ops lead  can now get night vigilance and perimeter from the fence and floor cams already there — without per-camera seats or another night shift. 
           A  captain or plant ops lead  can now know who’s onboard and who’s in zone when the link dies — on the cams already aboard or on site. 
         
       

       
         Powerful features 
         Platform reasons that cut across every persona — why EyeNet is not another camera cloud. 
       
         
           Any camera 
           Not vendor lock-in 
           Existing cams, phones, PCs — or inexpensive ordinary cameras. First detection in minutes on a ~16 GB PC. 
         
         
           Detect → decide → act 
           Not passive VMS 
           Targeted alerts to mobile, email, webhooks, signage, gates, and the ERP/CRM — only when something needs a person. 
         
         
           On-prem by default 
           Sovereignty + offline 
           Processing and footage stay on premises. Full operation when the internet is down; Matrix syncs on thin links. 
         
       

       
         
           No per-camera tax 
           Hardware-bound scale 
           Scale is the mesh you deploy — one room to a campus — not a per-camera license ceiling or a GPU farm. 
         
         
           Zero / near-zero hardware 
           Buy today 
           Staff use their own PC or mobile for presence grants; sites reuse cameras they already own. EyeNet scales to thousands of employees without a camera fleet project. 
         
         
           Six wedges, one fabric 
           Where it pays 
           HR presence, adaptive signage, home and away, Virtual Ward, night / perimeter security, shipping and industrial — Presence, Vradar, Sentinel, and Matrix on one stack.

title: What changes
text:
03  What changes  
 Users are not locked to a camera wall. The platform watches 24/7; the right person gets a targeted alert — mobile, email, webhook, clinical app, or HubSpot — only when something needs them. Ordinary cameras become an always-on assistant that decides and acts on premises, including when the internet is down. 

       
         
           Edge 
           Not cloud-bound 
           On-device AI. Full offline. Data sovereignty by default. Processing and storage stay on premises. 
         
         
           Action 
           Not passive VMS 
           Triggers fire mobile, email, webhooks, signage, and gates. Each camera has its own rules. 
         
         
           Scale 
           Hardware-bound 
           Any IP, WiFi, or phone camera. ~16 GB PC. One room to an enterprise mesh. No GPU farm. 
         
       

       
         
           Incumbents sell 
           
             Cloud storage & monthly bandwidth 
             Passive recordings & dashboards 
             Generic “AI boxes” 
             Projects that take quarters 
           
         
         
           EyeNet ships 
           
             On-prem decisions & zero video cloud 
             Targeted notifications that run the operation 
             Purpose-built apps for real jobs 
             Detection in minutes — scale by hardware 
           
         
       

       How it multiplies operator capacity 
       
          Vision nodes  — face, count, demographics, and routes on cameras the site already owns. 
          Entrances, restricted zones, VIP watchlists  — headcount, unauthorised presence, and person-of-interest alerts without extra posts. 
          Signage that reads the room  — age, gender, and group size switch content in milliseconds, with impressions and dwell. 
          Remote control from a phone  — VPN access to cameras, triggers, and dashboards. Footage stays on premises even when the operator does not.

title: Market validation

08  Market validation  
 FootfallCam is a successful, long-running commercial proof that buyers will pay for camera-based people analytics at scale. That is useful market validation for EyeNet — yet FootfallCam does not fully cover, and in several cases does not cover at all, EyeNet’s six vertical market segments. EyeNet’s wedge is sovereignty plus operational action across those six; FootfallCam’s wedge is retail and facility footfall BI. 

 
   
     Validation 
     FootfallCam shows a real paid market for edge people analytics — multi-year UK entity, partner channel, global installs. 
   
   
     Gap 
     Their primary industries (retail, malls, queues, washrooms, offices-as-occupancy) leave EyeNet’s six wedges largely open.

       Full B2C → B2B → Enterprise package ladder

      Dwell / route / behavioural paths   Yes  +  WIP  Route Behavioural Configurator (body routes + face cross-validation on same camera/time plane; target November 2026)   Yes  — heat dwell, heatmaps shipping today  
      Heatmaps / queues / desk occupancy suites  Heatmap  WIP ; queues  not documented ; desk suite  partial    Yes   
      Face / POI / watchlist   Yes    Different  — demographics, not security POI stack  
      Intrusion, fall/voice, PPE, guard vigilance   Yes    No   
      Attendance / Presence check-in   Yes  — face + QR/NFC   Different  — footfall, not HR check-in  
   
 
 
   EyeNet — Route Behavioural Configurator (WIP) 
   Worker in development: people-movement from body detection, known-body identity via face recognition cross-validated on the same route position / camera / time plane. Target ship November 2026 (final QA / ship-or-slip as of early November) — behavioural analytics parity with FootfallCam-style path/dwell metrics on EyeNet’s on-prem fabric. 
 

 4. Action & automation 
 
   
      Capability  EyeNet  FootfallCam  
   
   
      Rule engine / thresholds / alerts   Yes  — Vradar, per-camera triggers, AND/OR   Yes   
      Age / demographic trigger conditions   Yes    Partial   
      Mobile / email / SMS   Yes    Partial   
      Slack / Teams + general workflows   Yes  — simple user settings   Not documented  / custom pods  
      Vision-driven digital signage   Yes    No  as core product  
      Retail ops apps (roster, checkout, washroom)   Not documented  as packaged apps   Yes   
      Webhooks / gates / physical actions   Yes    Partial  — data webhooks; checkout alerts  
      Multi-site Matrix + VPN remote   Yes    Partial   
   
 

 Where each wins 
 
   
     EyeNet 
     
       Six use-case markets FootfallCam does not productise (HR Presence, Signage, cottage, Virtual Ward, night security, shipping/industrial + Sentinel) 
       On-prem vision that acts — age-band triggers, Slack/Teams workflows, OpenAPI/Swagger, pluggable storage 
       B2C → B2B → Enterprise package ladder; no per-camera license ceiling 
       Behavioural route parity via WIP configurator (target November 2026) 
     
   
   
     FootfallCam 
     
       Purpose-built retail/facility people-flow measurement shipping today (queues, staff exclusion, heatmaps, desk occupancy) 
       Packaged ops apps (roster, checkout, washroom, marketing ROI) 
       Mature multi-protocol data plane into BI / BMS 
     
   
 

 Business model & go-to-market 
 
   
      Dimension  EyeNet  FootfallCam  
   
   
      Primary motion   Full ladder  — B2C Light freemium → B2B Starter & Pro → Enterprise   Contact / consultative sales only  — demo, pilot, quote via sales or certified reseller; no self-serve checkout  
      How to buy  Web/app signup for Light; sales-assisted B2B; custom Enterprise  Consultancy → planning/quote → local distributor → install  
      Offer shape  Software packages on cameras you own; no per-camera licenses  Hardware counters + Centroid + V9; “starting at” then custom  
      Channel  Direct + partners (CRM, eHealth)  Global reseller / distributor network  
      Consumer / B2C   Yes  — B2C Light   Not offered   
   
 
 
   
      1  EyeNet packages 
     
        B2C Light  — freemium 60–90 days; Signage Lite $30–100/mo; Home Security Lite $20–50/mo; Retail Compliance Lite $50–100/mo; Event Security Lite $200–1,200/event 
        B2B Starter  — $500–1,000/mo · 1–5 locs · 5 cameras 
        B2B Professional  — $1,500–3,000/mo · 5–20 locs · 25 cameras · ACV path ~$12–36K/yr 
        Enterprise  — $5,000+/mo · Matrix · VPN fleets · custom integrations 
     
   
   
      2  FootfallCam packages 
     
       Retail Essentials / Standard / Enterprise from  $550 / $1,100 / $1,700  
       Mall Essentials / Standard / Enterprise from  $3,300 / $9,500 / $9,970  
       All paths still close via  contact sales  or local partner 
       No public B2C / self-serve consumer SKU 
     
   
 

 FootfallCam only — typical clients & installations 
 FootfallCam’s published client and install footprint only — used here as market-size colour for the validation thesis. 
 
    30,000+  Businesses supported with partners  
    500+  Named global clients; tens of thousands of counters  
    10,000+  Locations claimed worldwide  
 
 
   
     Segment mix (marketing) 
     
        2,200+  retailers 
        1,200+  mall operators 
        500+  offices 
        150+  bus / public transport 
     
   
   
     Typical install pattern 
     
       Pro2 counters at entrances (often 1–2 per retail door set) 
       Centroid reuses existing CCTV for zones / heatmaps / journey 
       Install via partner network, customer contractor, or guided self-install 
       Retail starting packages ~$550 / $1,100 / $1,700; malls ~$3,300 / $9,500 / $9,970 (still sales-led) 
     
   
 

 FootfallCam only — UK vs abroad install geography estimate 
 FootfallCam is  designed and manufactured in the UK  with UK/Malaysia ops centres, but public footprint claims describe a  global-majority  install base: deployments in  200+ countries ,  10,000+ locations , and a “global-domestic” reseller model. Named UK rollouts show a real home market; they do not read as the majority of volume versus worldwide partner installs. 
 
   
      UK ~⅕  
      Abroad ~⅘  
   
   Illustrative estimate from public footprint claims (not a disclosed UK/ROW revenue split). 
 

 
   
     Appendix — FootfallCam financials & staff (optional in live meetings) 
     Open for UK filing colour on the paid-market thesis. Lead the room with Validation / Gap / EyeNet six above. 
   

 FootfallCam only — financials (USD) 
 FOOTFALLCAM UK LIMITED public accounts only — colour on the validation thesis, not an EyeNet comparison table. 
 Unaudited abridged accounts. Converted at  ≈ $1.27 / £1 . Turnover / operating profit for 2019–2023 are third-party estimates. Net assets and cash through 2024 from filed-account extracts. No public VC rounds; company states zero external financing / zero debt; privately held 50/50 by founders.

   FootfallCam only — capital posture 
   No public venture or PE rounds. Growth funded from retained earnings. UK Companies House filings show ~6–9 employees on the UK entity — the figure that triangulates with the P&L above. Website “200+ employees” claims are addressed in the staff note below. 
 

 FootfallCam only — staff & partner ecosystem 
 Organisation and channel claims cross-checked against UK filings. Exact global reseller/distributor headcount is not disclosed. 

 
    ~6–9  Employees on UK Companies House filings (YE 2020–2025)  
    ~$11M  Est. YE 2023 turnover (UK entity)  
    200+ / 80+  Marketing claim on About page — treat with caution  
 

 
   Gentle note — headcount vs financials 
   FootfallCam’s About page states a team of  over 200 employees  (HQ and regional offices), including  80+ engineers . That claim does  not  line up cleanly with the UK legal entity’s public accounts: 
   
     FOOTFALLCAM UK LIMITED reports only  ~6 employees  for most recent years (about  9  in the latest Endole extract for YE 2025). 
     Estimated UK-entity turnover peaks near  $11M  (YE 2023). At 200 FTEs that would imply only ~ $55k revenue per employee  — thin for a hardware + analytics vendor, and hard to fund if a large share of roles were UK-costed. 
     Filed UK staff costs for ~6 people (order-of-magnitude ~$0.5M) fit a small UK core; they do  not  look like a 200-person payroll on that entity alone. 
   
   A fair reading is that  200+ / 80+  is likely a  marketing or group-wide framing  (possibly blending offshore teams, contractors, or partner capacity) rather than verified FTE on the UK books. Prefer the  filed UK headcount  for financial triangulation; treat the website staff figures as  overstated or at least not directly comparable  to the published P&L until a consolidated group disclosure appears. 
 

 
   
     What the filings support 
     
       Small UK entity headcount (~6–9) with meaningful net assets and cash 
       Ops narrative of UK + Malaysia centres — some delivery may sit outside the UK filing 
       Third-party aggregators sometimes show ~115–118 “employees” — still far below 200, and still not the UK statutory figure 
     
   
   
     Channel ecosystem (published roles)

        Technology / regional distributors  — stock, logistics, local invoicing; country/region exclusivity offered 
        System / enterprise integrators  — infrastructure and enterprise rollouts 
        Installation specialists & deployment partners  — on-site install, field deployment, maintenance 
        Consultants  — planning and project specification 
        Nationwide field-service partners

      10,000+ locations  worldwide 
      30,000+ businesses  supported together with partners 
     “Global-domestic” model: FootfallCam supplies the platform;  partners lead local sales, deployment, and support  
     Exact headcount of resellers / distributors / SI partners is  not published  as a single roster total

title: Project status
text:
09  Project status  
 Product readiness and partners from the July 2026 business-plan primer, plus the capital and growth path restated in the same seed-ladder language as sections 05–06. Team started July 2024; working prototype in under six months. Five of six products are beta-ready —  Sentinel  (wearables / drones) remains in active build. Status as of 7 November 2026. 

       The six products 
       
         
           
             Product 
             Job 
             Status 
           
         
         
           
              EyeNet Presence  
             Automatic attendance with face + QR/NFC check-in. Replaces paper timesheets and badge swipes. 
              Beta  
           
           
              EyeNet Signage  
             Digital screens that change content based on who is watching (age, gender). Measurable advertising. 
              Beta  
           
           
              EyeNet Vradar  
             Alert brain: rules such as crowd thresholds that fire mobile, email, or other actions. Powers the rest of the stack. 
              Beta  
           
           
              EyeNet Gate  
             Entrance and exit monitoring. Counts people in and out; flags suspicious faces in real time. 
              Beta  
           
           
              EyeNet Sentinel  
             Wearable camera glasses + drones for VIP / bodyguard teams. Spots persons of interest in a crowd. 
              Active build  
           
           
              EyeNet Matrix  
             One dashboard across dozens of sites. Franchise chains, shipping fleets, multi-location businesses. 
              Beta  
           
         
       
       Status as of 7 November 2026: Presence, Signage, Vradar, Gate, and Matrix are beta-ready with design partners. Sentinel (wearables / drones) is the remaining active-build product. 

       Current milestones 
       
          July 2024:  Working prototype delivered in under six months. 
          Q3 2026 → now:  Five of six products beta-ready with design partners; Sentinel remains in active build (as of November 2026). 
          Two distribution partners signed:  TMA / Talos (TMAIX) — EyeNet-branded channel — and NewGen Group (white-label). Both early-stage, pursuing hot leads across municipalities, enterprises, and maritime clients. 
          Deloitte engagement:  NewGen has laid groundwork for a demo with Deloitte Greece and a path to the Deloitte EMEA Cyber Security Committee. The tentative September 2026 committee slot has passed; outcome / next date TBD as of November 2026. 
          LG International hot lead:  TMA / Talos is positioning EyeNet for a European municipality and has identified a high-potential early-stage lead with LG International — major upside if it converts. 
       

       Capital and growth path 
       Same seed ladder as section 05: burn floor first, then how much speed to buy. Extra capital does not rewrite unit economics — it buys speed and makes way for a sooner and bigger exit. Instrument: convertible note or SAFE across scenarios. 

       
         
           
             Horizon 
             Plan 
           
         
         
           
              Seed · Burn floor · $500K  
             Year-1 ops floor: launch, first pilots, lean runway. Personnel / marketing / tech / ops covered; Greek unit as EU pilot. Typical next: Series A / growth ~$700K–$1M after traction. 
           
           
              Seed · Base · $1M  
             Burn covered, plus fuller GTM. Plan terms: ~25% at $3M pre ($4M post). Target: 5–10 pilots, $50–100K ARR, 50-lead pipeline, 2–3 partners; formal Greek + U.S. units. Typical next: Series A $2–3M on $8–12M pre (target window through H1 2027). 
           
           
              Seed · Accelerate · $2.5M  
             Same core economics, earlier scale: denser sales and multi-site footprint in the seed window; Greek + U.S. units and London representation. Series A still available for land-and-expand; larger seed compresses time to that raise. 
           
           
              Series A  
             Size and timing scale with seed choice: ~$700K–$1M after burn-floor traction; $2–3M on the base path; larger seed still leaves Series A for land-and-expand. Use of proceeds: dedicated sales, marketing ramp, path toward ~200 customers. 
           
           
              2027  
             ~$1M revenue · 50 B2B · ~600 consumer users — first commercial proof after seed launch of the five beta-ready products. 
           
           
              2028  
             ~$8M revenue · 200 B2B · 6,000+ consumer — breakeven. Capital above burn accelerates arrival; unit economics stay the same. 
           
           
              2029  
             ~$26M revenue · 500 B2B · 20,000+ consumer — solidly profitable on the three motions (B2C Light, B2B Starter / Pro, Enterprise). 
           
           
              2030–2031  
             Exit path: IPO or strategic acquisition at $500M–$1B (plan target range). 
           
         
       

       Why this path is underwritable 
       
          Products are built, not imagined:  Five of six apps exist as working beta (Sentinel still in active build). Capital on the seed ladder buys selling what works — computer vision, recognition, and alert automation are already done — not building from scratch. 
          Distribution is already on board:  TMA / Talos (TMAIX) and NewGen are signed partners pursuing leads, not letters of intent. That de-risks the first ~50 paying customers and the base-seed pipeline target. 
          Deloitte is a force multiplier in waiting:  Groundwork for Deloitte Greece / EMEA Cyber Security Committee is in place; September 2026 slot passed — confirm outcome or next date in diligence. 
          LG International is a global-scale multiplier:  Early-stage hot lead, not a closed deal. A win with LG’s trading and investment arm can unlock manufacturing, logistics, retail, and government supply-chain distribution and open other Korean / Asian conglomerate doors. 
          Burn floor first, then speed:  Underwrite $500K ops, then choose $1M or $2.5M for how fast footprint and GTM stand up. CAC, LTV, and payback in How it is sold hold across all three seed scenarios. 
       
       Seed scenarios and footprint detail: sections 05–06. TAM share, CAC / LTV, and package pricing: How it is sold and Addendum B. Growth years and exit ranges from eyenet-web/bp/onepager/primer.html (July 2026), restated on the seed ladder.
